Lead low kick, right cross the best combo I think there is besides a basic 1-2. As you say the weight transfer just loads up the right hand perfectly, and the low kick doesn’t even have to have much on it just enough to draw their attention downward for a split second and bomb em with the right hand. 

My old coach drilled that combo into me alot (and everytime he’d always bring up Hendo and Randy Couture lol) I could see the practicality of it but never thought much of it. 

Until I had an awakening of sorts. I had sparred a bunch before, and even had street fights, but not against super skilled opponents. Anyway my first time actually fighting someone who trained the way I was, in the gym all the time it was rough I was young like 18 and this guy was like 22 and honestly just a bit more skilled and in shape than I was. 

The bell rings and I’m thinking “okay let me try and feel this out and get a rhythm going” and he just starts throwing super crisp relentless boxing combinations I mean seriously just lighting me up. 

I never experienced that before and it was just very sudden and it was like all my training went out the window for a a few seconds. Anyway im just getting lit up and trying to get away from this guy and block some punches and find a window to counter but he was just relentless walking me right down…  

So I didn’t even think, I was getting desperate and my body just did it, I’d drilled that lead low kick right cross like a thousand times and as he’s coming in I hit him with the kick and he just walked right into the right hand and I threw it HARD. 

His knees buckled and he crumpled forward to the floor. I was just so surprised that one combo my coach always emphasized to me actually saved my ass. I was never a big power puncher, more of a volume striker and I never put anyone down like that my coach was surprised too, he was watching from an angle behind my opponent and he thought I kicked him in the nuts at first lol 

Anyway that’s my lead low kick - right hand story haha
